findings.key_quote: Three direct customers accounted for 25 %, 18 %, and 13 % of our accounts receivable balance as of January 25, 2026. Two direct customers accounted for 17 % and 16 % of our accounts receivable balance as of January 26, 2025.
findings.justification: This evidence shows the concentration of accounts receivable at two different dates (January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025), which are instant measurements. While this provides information about the composition of accounts receivable, it does not directly address whether the growth in accounts receivable signals deteriorating collection quality. The concentration percentages alone do not establish collection quality metrics.

This shows the allowance for doubtful accounts remained flat at $4 million for fiscal year 2026 (same as fiscal year 2025), which is a metric related to collection quality. However, this is only one component of collection quality and does not by itself establish whether the growth in accounts receivable signals deteriorating collection quality. The flat allowance could suggest stable collection quality, but without knowing the absolute level of accounts receivable growth or other collection metrics (like days sales outstanding), this evidence alone does not decide the assertion.

findings.key_quote: our extended payment term arrangements with certain customers, the inability of some customers to make required payments, our ability to obtain credit insurance for customers with extended payment terms, and customer bad debt write-offs
